citation.title: The Effect of Acute Hyperglycaemia Induced by Oral Glucose Load on Heart Rate Variability and Skin Microvascular Reactivity in Healthy Young Adults

population.description: Twenty healthy young volunteers (15 males, 5 females, females in the follicular phase), non-smokers, all with a normal BMI (no BMI numbers printed), no medication. Age 21.6 +/- 1.6 y as printed (Methods 2.1; the +/- is taken as SD, Methods 2.6 says mean +/- SD).

protocols.name: fasted_arrival
protocols.description: Capillary fasting sample taken on arrival, before any measurement, after 12 h with water only; a 30-minute fasted run-in stands for the single sample, read at minute 30

protocols.name: ogtt_75g
protocols.description: 75 g glucose in 250 mL water drunk over 5 min after 12 h with water only; capillary sample on arrival (minute 0), 30 min acclimatisation, 10 min baseline + 3 min occlusion + 10 min normalisation, then the drink: 30+10+3+10 = 53 min after the arrival sample (Methods 2.4); capillary sample 30 min after the drink = minute 83 (30 min counted from the start of drinking); the minute-53 load time and the minute-83 sample are derived by adding the printed durations, so duration_min and the meal time are assumed (the 75 g and the 12 h fast are printed)

findings.description: Fasting capillary glucose (HemoCue, the paper's cglc) on arrival before the OGTT trial; mean +/- SD (Methods 2.6)

location.quote: Fasting cglc (before any provocation) obtained from the capillary blood sample was 5.0 mM ± 0.4 mM pre-OGTT

findings.description: Capillary glucose 30 min after the 75 g drink minus the arrival fasting sample (minute 0 to minute 83); mean +/- SD (Methods 2.6)

location.quote: cglc increased for 2.2 mM ± 0.5 mM after OGTT

left_out.what: venous glucose and serum insulin changes from fasting at 30, 50, 90 min after the 75 g OGTT, and fasting venous glucose 4.3 +/- 0.3 mM and insulin 2.6 +/- 1.9 uU/mL (Table 4, Results 3.3): the separate kinetics trial never states how many participants it had
capillary glucose at the end of the haemodynamic measurements (50 min) and the post-OGTT absolute value (Figure 1 only); water-control glucose is not shown

resting haemodynamics before and the changes after OGTT or water: R-R interval, blood pressures, laser Doppler flux, LF, HF, LF/HF, PORH parameters (Tables 1 and 2) are medians with interquartile ranges

low-glucose (rise <2.3 mM) and high-glucose (>=2.3 mM) groups, and correlations of HRV and PORH changes with the glucose rise (Table 3, Figures 2-3): groups are formed from the glucose measurement itself
